title: Normalized slice evaluation for continuous coefficient inverse image
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For any scheme $W$, use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the continuous coefficient sheaves $A_W(V)=C(|V|,A)$, $E_W(V)=C(|V|,E)$ with constant-section normalization [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients, lem-weil-pbc-continuous-ring-functions-sheaf]. For a noetherian finite-dimensional $X$ with $\ell$ invertible these identify with $B_X=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_X$ and $B_X[1/\varpi]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. Let $u:U\to X$ be any object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with no noetherian hypothesis on $U$. Under the localization equivalence $U_{\mathrm{proet}}\simeq X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$ [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], the inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is canonically the slice restriction $F|_U(V\to U)=F(V\to X)$. It sends the continuous integral and rational coefficient rings to $A_U,E_U$, identically on the continuous functions of the same underlying $V$. It preserves every finite constant quotient, its quotient transitions and the coefficient projections. In the inverse-image indexing category $\mathcal I_V$ this identification is induced by the initial object $(V\to X,(s,\mathrm{id}_V))$, where $s:V\to U$ is the structure map; thus it is normalized for the actual inverse-image construction, including its sheafification. Module restriction is exact and its derived functor is termwise restriction [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence]. In particular, for an etale morphism $g:X'\to X$ between schemes with the same hypotheses the finite-quotient structural maps are isomorphisms $g^{-1}B_X\cong B_{X'}$, $g^{-1}E_X\cong E_{X'}$, and $E_{X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}E_X}g^{-1}(-)$ is exact ordinary inverse image. The same conclusion holds for a locally closed immersion by the specified immersion coefficient isomorphisms. Site restriction of an ambient derived pullback is the corresponding restricted module pullback; all these identifications preserve coefficient maps and constant sections.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], composition with $u$ identifies $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$, including coverings. Hence the sheaf $F|_U$ of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] has values $F(V\to X)$ and restrictions $F(b)$ on arrows $b:V^{\prime}\to V$ over $U$. This applies to sets, abelian groups, rings and modules over the restricted ring; neither the equivalence nor this description requires $U$ to be noetherian.

proof.text: Compute the construction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] at $s:V\to U$. An object of $\mathcal I_V$ is $(W\to X,\phi:V\to U\times_XW)$; write $a=\operatorname{pr}_W\phi$, so $\phi=(s,a)$. By clause (1) of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], applied to the site object $u:U\to X$, the object $i_0=(V\to X,(s,\mathrm{id}_V))$ is initial in $\mathcal I_V$, its unique arrow to $(W,\phi)$ being $a:V\to W$; the coprojections at these objects give an isomorphism of presheaves $F|_U\cong u_{u,p}F$, natural in $F$, and the sheafification unit $u_{u,p}F\to u^{-1}F$ is an isomorphism, for sheaves of sets, abelian groups and rings. Explicitly, since $i_0$ is terminal in $\mathcal I_V^{\mathrm{op}}$, the inverse of the coprojection at $i_0$ sends the coprojection of $z\in F(W)$ to $F(a)(z)$. For $b:V^{\prime}\to V$ over $U$, replacing $a$ by $ab$ gives $F(ab)=F(b)F(a)$, so these isomorphisms agree with the restriction maps of Step 1. By the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] the identification $u^{-1}F\cong F|_U$ is the unique extension of this presheaf isomorphism across the sheafification unit. This proves the asserted normalization for the actual inverse image, not merely existence of an abstract isomorphism.

proof.text: For $T=A,E$, [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-ring-functions-sheaf] supplies the sheaf $T_W(V)=C(|V|,T)$ on every scheme $W$. Its restrictions are precomposition by definition [def-weil-pbc-lisse-lattice-coefficients]. For the continuous coefficient structural map, a representative $z:|W|\to T$ at $(W,(s,a))$ maps to $z\circ |a|$. Indeed its direct-image adjoint first pulls $z$ back along $U\times_XW\to W$, and then evaluation along $(s,a)$ gives precisely this function. At $i_0$ it is $z$ itself. Thus the identification in Step 2 sends $u^{-1}T_X$ to $T_U$ identically on functions and respects pointwise operations. For every continuous coefficient homomorphism $h:T\to T^{\prime}$, the equality $h\circ(z\circ |a|)=(h\circ z)\circ |a|$ proves compatibility with coefficient postcomposition. It applies to $A\to E$ and $A\to A/\varpi^n$. A constant function remains the same constant. For each finite discrete ring $A/\varpi^n$, [lem-pur-proetale-finite-constant-sections] gives ring isomorphisms $\theta_{W,V}:(A/\varpi^n)_W(V)\cong C(|V|,A/\varpi^n)$ on every scheme $W$, sending constants to constants and compatible with precomposition; so the coefficient projection $A_W\to(A/\varpi^n)_W$ is postcomposition with $A\to A/\varpi^n$ followed by $\theta^{-1}$. Under Step 2, $\theta_{X}$ and $\theta_U$ are both evaluated on the same $V$, so they correspond. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (equivalently clause (2) of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction]) identifies restriction of the constant sheaf with the constant sheaf on $U$ by this constant-section map. Its uniqueness proves that quotient transitions also commute. Hence the coefficient projections are preserved as sheaf maps, including their sheafification units.

proof.text: For the noetherian $X$ of the statement, [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] identifies $B_X$ with $A_X$ and its sheaf localization at $\varpi$ with $E_X$. Combining these identifications with Steps 2-3 gives $u^{-1}B_X\cong A_U$ and $u^{-1}E_X\cong E_U$. In particular this is not an assertion that an arbitrary inverse image commutes with an infinite limit: here slice restriction is evaluation on the same $V$, so it preserves the sectionwise inverse-limit cone. The projections of the restricted cone are exactly the projections in Step 3. The localization comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence] sends $z/\varpi^r$ to the restricted $z$ divided by the same constant $\varpi^r$, so its rational coefficient identification agrees with Step 3. No noetherian assertion about $U$ was used.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2), pp. 58-59; sites-modules.tex Tags 03EL/03CZ, coefficient localization

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence] to the geometric morphism of Step 2 and either coefficient ring: module inverse image over its inverse-image ring is exact and its derived functor is termwise inverse image, with no bound on the complex. Since Step 3 identifies that ring with the continuous coefficient ring on $U$, module restriction is exact and is derived termwise. More explicitly, whenever a structural coefficient map $c:g^{-1}R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ is an isomorphism, the scalar-extension map $S\otimes_{g^{-1}R}g^{-1}M\to g^{-1}M$, $b\otimes m\mapsto c^{-1}(b)m$, has inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ after transporting the module action along $c$. The balancing relation proves the two identities. Consequently extension of scalars along $c$ is exact, and its derived tensor is this same inverse image on complexes. The cited comparison commutes with the specified ring identification, so all coefficient normalizations from Steps 3-4 persist on modules and derived categories.

source.place: Tags 03EL/03CZ, tensor pullback and scalar adjunction; exact inverse image over the pulled-back ring

proof.text: For an etale $g:X^{\prime}\to X$, [def-weil-etale-morphism] says that $g$ is flat and unramified, and [def-weil-unramified-morphism] gives an open diagonal. An open immersion identifies local rings by [def-weil-open-immersion], hence is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism] (a ring is free of rank one over itself). Thus $g$ has flat diagonal and is weakly etale by [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism], so $X^{\prime}\to X$ is a site object. Apply Steps 2-5 with $U=X^{\prime}$. Both schemes are noetherian by hypothesis, so Step 4 on each of them gives the stated isomorphisms $g^{-1}B_X\cong B_{X^{\prime}}$ and $g^{-1}E_X\cong E_{X^{\prime}}$ with the finite-quotient maps of Step 3. Step 5 then gives the displayed derived-tensor formula as exact ordinary inverse image. For a locally closed immersion $g$, use instead the isomorphisms induced by pullback of continuous functions in [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction], and apply Step 5 to its geometric inverse image. Those maps preserve constants and commute with coefficient projections because both are postcomposition of continuous functions. This proves the immersion assertion without treating a closed immersion as a pro-etale site object.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15, p. 62, etale and closed-immersion inverse image; paragraph before Definition 6.8.6, p. 60; weakly etale criterion by flatness and flat diagonal

proof.text:
Finally let $f:Y\to X$ be an ambient morphism and $j:U\to Y$ a site object. Write $R=f^{-1}E_X$ and $H=f^{-1}$, so the ambient pullback is $E_Y\otimes_R^L HK$. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback], applied first to $(H,\mathrm{id}_R)$ and then to slice restriction over $R|_U$, both $HP$ and $(HP)|_U$ are K-flat with flat terms over their respective rings. The computation in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] therefore represents ambient pullback by $E_Y\otimes_R HP$, and restricted module pullback by $E_U\otimes_{R|_U}(HP)|_U$. Step 5 allows exact restriction of the first representative. Apply [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] in each degree to the two $R$-modules $E_Y$ and $HP^n$, and Step 3 to $E_Y|_U=E_U$. This gives
$$ (E_Y\otimes_R^L HK)|_U\cong E_U\otimes_{R|_U}^L(HK)|_U. $$
The cited tensor comparison sends the sheafification image of $b\otimes m$ to the image of the identical tensor. Its naturality makes the degreewise maps commute with differentials and with maps of resolutions; the cited derived-pullback computation makes them independent of the resolution. This is the corresponding restricted module pullback, even when $U$ is not noetherian. The same formula with $A$ proves the integral version. Coefficient projections, coefficient inclusion and constant sections commute with these maps because the tensor representatives are unchanged and Step 3 already checked coefficient postcomposition.
